title: Check yourself: placing a missing answer and explaining a day

questions.stem: A purchase from terminal 29110044 timed out at 09:41:27, twenty seconds after your log shows its bytes written to the acquirer's link. The next day the acquirer reports that its log holds no trace of that message. What should your switch have done at 09:41:27, and what needs fixing?

options.text: Reversed the purchase, since it had left your side; the link between the two logs needs fixing
options.says: a request that left is reversed wherever it stopped, even when the host's log shows nothing; bytes written on one side and nothing logged on the other place the loss between the two logs

options.text: Reversed the purchase, since it had left your side; the acquirer's host, which dropped it, needs fixing
options.says: the host's log has no trace of the request, so the host never received it; the loss is between the logs, not in the host

options.text: Sent it again as a new purchase, since it never reached the host; the link between the two logs needs fixing
options.says: at the timeout the switch can't know where the request stopped; only a request that never left may go again, and this one had left

options.text: Sent it again as a new purchase, since it never reached the host; the acquirer's host, which dropped it, needs fixing
options.says: the request had left, so it is reversed rather than sent again, and a host that never logged it did not drop it

origin.section: 15.3. A Missing Answer Is Placed by the Last Log That Saw the Message

questions.stem: Since Tuesday's upgrade, every purchase your switch sends through one acquirer times out, and the acquirer's portal shows the purchases approved. Your team pulls one finding from the logs and draws one conclusion. Which pair holds?

options.text: An answer in your own log that matched no request, so the fields your switch pairs on are the place to look
options.says: an answer that reached you and matched nothing differs from its request in a pairing field; that is what to compare

options.text: An answer in your own log that matched no request, so the acquirer's host is the place to look
options.says: the host answered and the answer reached you; the place is your side, the timeout or the pairing fields

options.text: An answer in the acquirer's log marked as sent, so the fields your switch pairs on are the place to look
options.says: an answer sent by the host proves nothing about your side until your own log shows it arrived; with nothing in yours, the link is the place

options.text: An answer in the acquirer's log marked as sent, so the acquirer's host is the place to look
options.says: a host that logged its answer as sent did answer; the answer stopped after it, on the link or on your side

origin.section: 15.3.1. Spot the Problem: The Terminal Whose Approvals Never Arrived

questions.stem: Sunday's total is 2,310.40 in your records and in the acquirer's settlement report. Matched by terminal and RRN, one purchase is 64.00 in your records and 40.00 in the report, and the report holds a 24.00 purchase your records lack. What follows for these two purchases?

options.text: Neither of them needs work, since the differences cancel and the day's money is right
options.says: money moves per transaction: the 40.00 purchase leaves a merchant short and the 24.00 one charges a cardholder, whatever the total

options.text: Neither of them needs work, since equal totals mean both sides hold the same purchases
options.says: the totals agree while the report holds a purchase the switch lacks; equal totals can hide differences that cancel

options.text: Both of them need work, since each leaves a merchant or a cardholder with the wrong amount
options.says: a day that balances can hold pairs of differences that cancel; each is explained transaction by transaction

options.text: Both of them need work, since the acquirer's report must have counted one purchase twice
options.says: a purchase only in the network's report is usually an approval after a timeout that was never reversed, not a purchase counted twice

origin.section: 15.4. A Difference in Totals Is Explained Transaction by Transaction, Even When the Totals Agree

questions.stem: A purchase of 120.00 was answered with field 39 set to 10 and 75.00 approved. Your switch booked 120.00 and told the terminal the purchase was approved. Who is out of pocket, and by how much?

options.text: The merchant, by 45.00, since it handed over 120.00 of goods and is paid for 75.00
options.says: code 10 is a partial approval; booked at the requested amount, the terminal shows a full approval and the merchant is paid only what the issuer approved

options.text: The merchant, by 120.00, since a partial approval is paid out like a decline
options.says: a partial approval moves the approved amount; the merchant is paid 75.00

options.text: The cardholder, by 45.00, since the card is charged the 120.00 the switch booked
options.says: the issuer charges what it approved, 75.00; the switch's booking moves no money

options.text: The cardholder, by 120.00, since both the approved and the requested amounts are charged
options.says: only the approved amount is charged; the difference falls on the merchant

origin.section: 15.4. A Difference in Totals Is Explained Transaction by Transaction, Even When the Totals Agree
